parts.role: Runs the firmware and supplies 3.3 V from its USB-powered regulator.
Shows the time left in the session.
Turn to set the time; press to start or pause.

nets.name: +3V3
nets.why: One 3.3 V supply from the ESP32 board’s regulator. Every part here runs at 3.3 V, so its signals match the ESP32’s 3.3 V logic.

nets.name: GND
nets.why: Common ground. Every signal is measured against it, so every part must share it.

nets.name: I2C_SCL
nets.why: I²C clock, driven by the ESP32. GPIO22 is the default SCL pin of the ESP32 Arduino Wire library. Most breakouts already carry pull-up resistors.

nets.name: I2C_SDA
nets.why: I²C data, in both directions. GPIO21 is the default SDA pin of the ESP32 Arduino Wire library.

nets.name: ENC_A
nets.why: Encoder channel A (CLK). With channel B it tells which way the knob turned: whichever changes first gives the direction.

nets.name: ENC_B
nets.why: Encoder channel B (DT), read alongside channel A. GPIO32 and 33 are plain input/output pins with no boot role.

nets.name: ENC_SW
nets.why: The knob’s push switch connects this pin to ground when pressed. Enable INPUT_PULLUP on GPIO27 so it reads high when released.

nets.name: BUZZER
nets.why: GPIO23 toggles a tone (for example with ledcWriteTone) and the piezo clicks at that frequency. A passive piezo draws very little current, so the pin can drive it directly.

notes.text: This board expects GND-VCC-SCL-SDA. Check yours before plugging it in.
Power the encoder from 3V3, not 5V: its pull-ups would otherwise put 5 V on ESP32 inputs.
Use a passive piezo transducer. A magnetic or active buzzer needs a transistor driver, which is not drawn here.
